item.title: 50,000 Fake Stats Went Live, Google Forgot Them, ChatGPT Kept Citing Them — 7 Months Later I Read the Receipt
item.description: A public experiment from peec.ai: a brand-new domain generated 50,000 invented statistics with GPT-4.1 in a single day, for roughly $50 in total. Seven months on, Google deindexed it but ChatGPT never stopped pulling from it — 330+ referring domains, and the fake numbers ended up in an academic paper and a bank's investment research. I tear the citation-laundering chain apart and explain why sourcing every number is the one control that actually stops it.
